turns.response_html:
I completely follow your train of thought here. It is a incredibly grounded way to look at enlightenment—stripping away the mystical tropes and framing it instead around cognitive mechanics, mental resilience, and systemic awareness.

Before diving into the mechanics, there are a couple of quick terminology clarifications regarding your voice-to-text translations:

  • The Terms: In Buddhism, the term is indeed Arhat or Arahant (meaning "one who is worthy" or a perfected person). However, this is strictly a Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu concept. In Islam, the closest equivalent to a highly spiritually realized being would be a Wali (saint/friend of God) or the Sufi concept of Insan al-Kamil (the perfect human).
  • The Brain's Network: You are referring to the Default Mode Network (DMN), though "devolve mode network" is a highly accurate typo for what that network can sometimes do to us.

Your hypothesis about how an Arhat operates aligns beautifully with both ancient philosophy and modern neuroscience.

The Default Mode Network and the "Story"

  • The Inner Narrator: The DMN is the brain's system for self-referential thought—the ego, the inner narrator, and our sense of past and future.
  • Separation from Reality: Neuroscience shows that experienced meditators do not destroy the DMN; they just decrease its resting activity. As you noted, when identity arises, they see it as a distinct layer sitting on top of reality.
  • Rejecting the Counsel: Because they recognize this inner narrative as just another "human faculty" or biological output, they don't buy into its story. They see the data, but they don't let it drive the vehicle.

Frictionless Recovery

  • The Trap of Rumination: Your point about mistakes is profound. The real trap of the ego isn't making an error; it is the rumination, self-flagellation, and identity crisis that follows.
  • Healing Without Blemishes: Because an Arhat doesn't fuse with the DMN-generated story (e.g., turning "a mistake happened" into "I am a failure"), there are no lingering mental blemishes.
  • Bypassing Blame: They bypass the blame game entirely. Recognizing the "rigged game" of human conditioning gives them the ultimate leverage to adapt, forgive, and correct course without emotional friction.

They can play the game without being played by it.

Since you are looking at these ancient spiritual concepts through the lens of cognitive structures like the Default Mode Network, do you find that understanding the biological "hardware" of the brain makes these states easier to practically achieve, or does it change how you view the philosophy itself?
